title: Which air fryer fits a family of four? The four-dish worksheet
question: Capacity claims versus the four dinners you actually cook
sections:
## What the format states, in its own words

The listing describes two independent baskets with a Sync Finish function and two viewing windows, and its specification table states a temperature range of 200–450 °F and 120 volts / 1700 watts. Its capacity field is one of the numbers the register marks as contested: the page talks about 6 quarts combined while its measurements table prints 6 liters, so both figures are published here and neither is chosen. A household that cooks a main and a side together is the household this format serves; a household that cooks one dish at a time should read the single-basket option instead.

Measure the gap before you compare capacities

Depth is the line that disqualifies a counter. The dual-basket unit states 13.38 inches deep, the single 8-quart 12.75 inches, and the oven-style unit 16.9 inches with French doors that need room in front as well as behind. A cavity you cannot install is not a cavity, and none of this is a question about brand.

What this worksheet will not do

We have not cooked in any of these units, so no minute appears on this page. What we can print is what the listings state and where they contradict themselves: the oven-style listing prints 24 presets in its title and 25 in its bullets, and it states no item weight at all, so those two fields stay contested rather than tidy. Links to the listings are affiliate links, marked as paid.
